input: Adsorption is widely regarded as an effective and versatile technique for removing dyes from wastewater, and metal-organic frameworks have attracted considerable attention as adsorbents due to their exceptionally high surface areas. In this study, the adsorption of a dye from water on a metal-organic framework was measured in a series of batch tests conducted at 298 K. Each test was carried out by contacting a known mass of adsorbent with the dye solution and measuring the concentration remaining in solution after the stated contact time. The experimental data were fitted to the Langmuir isotherm model, giving a fitted capacity of 256 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 6. Furthermore, at an adsorbent dose of 1 g L⁻¹, the removal after 120 min reached 83% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L⁻¹, corresponding to a residual concentration of just 8.5 mg L⁻¹. These results highlight the considerable potential of the framework as an adsorbent for dye removal, and the combination of a high capacity with rapid removal is particularly encouraging. It is important to note, however, that the Langmuir fit is reported for pH 6 only, and the capacity at other pH values was not measured. As a result, caution should be exercised when extrapolating the findings to other conditions, and further work would be required to fully characterise the performance of the material across a broader range of pH values.
target:
Adsorption of a dye from water on a metal-organic framework was measured in batch tests at 298 K. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 256 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 6. At an adsorbent dose of 1 g L⁻¹, removal after 120 min was 83% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L⁻¹, leaving a residual concentration of 8.5 mg L⁻¹.

The fitted capacity is an equilibrium property of the isotherm fit: it states the loading the surface approaches as the solution concentration rises, not the loading reached in the stated batch test. The batch removal and the isotherm capacity answer different questions. Removal reports what one dose achieved in one contact time, while capacity bounds what the solid can hold at equilibrium. The removal figure belongs to the stated dose and contact time together; a lower dose or a shorter contact time leaves more dye in solution. The residual concentration is the quantity a discharge limit would be set against, and it is fixed by the removal and the initial concentration together. Reporting the two results together fixes the conditions under which the removal was obtained and the equilibrium limit the removal is measured against. The Langmuir fit is reported for pH 6 only. Capacity at other pH values was not measured, and the stated capacity cannot be carried to a water of a different pH: adsorption of a dye on a framework depends on the charge state of both, and pH sets that state. The capacity and the removal were obtained in batch tests at one temperature, and the results state what the adsorbent achieved under those conditions.
